items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I didn't know any of Horace's musicians well... he told me that he was Rex Steward, a trumpet player that had taken Joe Smith's place in Fletcher's band.

ctx.x: I was at the Crystal and Horace's boys with Freddie Jenkins, Joe and Casper McCord and Red Hicks on trombone were sounding real great. Fletcher gave Horace quite a few of his arrangemnts and Horace came close to playing them almost like Fletcher. There was a little fat brown-skin guy that was standing against the wall near the band stand who looked like he was mad at the world and only smiled occasionally when one of the musicians in the band looked his way.

I didn't know any of Horace's musicians well, but I talked with some of them the same as I had done with other musicians that I didn't know very well. So I asked one of the musicians at the intermission who the little fat salty looking guy was, and he told me that he was Rex Steward, a trumpet player that had taken Joe Smith's place in Fletcher's band.

Sunday night I was at the Armory to hear Fletcher Henderson's orchestra for the second time. Naturally my place was right in front of the orchestra which was placed on the floor in the middle of the Armory. There was not a band stand because it was not a place where dances were given and the only one that I know of, that did take place there, was this dance that Fletcher was playing this night.
